shots.scene: South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A small south Indian railway station platform at hot noon, a black steam locomotive with third-class wooden coaches standing still, a few passengers in dhotis and sarees, station name board blank.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Inside an old third-class railway coach with wooden bench seats, a large bottle-green painted steel trunk tucked on the floor under a wooden bench seat, passengers nearby covering their noses with cloth and stepping back.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A police constable in 1950s khaki uniform with shorts and a red-banded turban cap kneeling beside a large green steel trunk, lifting its lid, his face shocked, light glowing from inside the trunk, the inside of the trunk not visible.
Still life with no people: an old brown paper case file tied with red tape lying on a wooden desk beside a pair of round spectacles and an inkpot, plain dark wall behind.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A busy 1950s Madras street corner with colonial red brick buildings, a tram, hand-pulled rickshaws, bullock carts and shop awnings in morning light.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Still life with no people: close view of a glass shop counter filled with neat rows of fountain pens in open boxes and small ink bottles, wooden shelves behind.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A middle-aged south Indian salesman of about forty with a moustache, white shirt and dhoti, standing behind a pen shop counter, smiling, holding out a fountain pen.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A sepia old photograph in a wooden frame of a young Indian soldier in a 1940s British Indian army khaki uniform standing straight.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Inside a small pen shop, a young south Indian woman of twenty-two in a simple cotton saree with a long plait looking at a fountain pen in her hand, across the counter a clean-shaven-chinned middle-aged salesman with only a thick moustache, white shirt, smiling politely.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A simple 1950s Kerala style wedding, a young bride in a cream saree and a slim young groom in white shirt and mundu with garlands, a few relatives around.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Empty street view with no people: a small whitewashed house with a red tiled roof and a wooden door on a quiet narrow lane near the sea, a long compound wall in the distance, evening light.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Inside a dark 1950s cinema hall, light from the screen on a young couple sitting side by side, the woman speaking with her head lowered, the man's face tense and angry.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Inside an old colonial police station, an inspector's wooden desk with registers and an inkpot, a constable writing a complaint in a big ledger.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A tall south Indian police inspector in 1950s khaki uniform and peaked cap questioning two shop assistants inside a pen shop, a notebook in his hand.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A small town hospital room, an elderly doctor in a white coat writing a report at a table, a closed green steel trunk on the floor in the corner.
A lonely unmarked earth mound with a small stone at the edge of a dry village field under a cloudy sky, palm trees far away.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A police inspector sitting in a cane chair in the morning reading a folded newspaper with wide alert eyes, a steel tumbler of coffee on a side table.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Two policemen in khaki forcing open a locked wooden door of a small tiled house, neighbours watching from a distance.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. An empty bare room of an old house with no furniture, a policeman in khaki holding a torch, its round beam lighting a small faint brown smudge low on a whitewashed wall.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A thin dark south Indian rickshaw puller, bare-headed with short hair, wearing a vest and a checked lungi, standing beside his hand-pulled rickshaw and pointing towards the sea while talking to a police inspector in khaki.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A beach at dusk with fishing boats, seen from far away the dark silhouette of a man near the waves throwing a round cloth bundle into the sea, a rickshaw waiting on the sand.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A big colonial railway station at night with gas lamps, a porter in a red shirt carrying a large green steel trunk on his head towards a waiting train, a man with a bandaged hand walking beside him seen from behind.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A beach at evening, a police constable in khaki standing frozen in shock looking down at something hidden behind a small sand ridge near the waves, the object not visible.
Two old paper case files lying side by side on a wooden desk under a hanging lamp, a magnifying glass between them.
A police inspector standing in deep thought with a hand on his chin, large question marks drawn in the dark background around him.
A police inspector looking straight at the viewer and pointing a finger forward, serious questioning expression, plain dark background.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A grand old colonial medical college building with arches and a clock tower, students in white walking in front, daylight.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A 1950s laboratory, two Indian doctors in white coats and spectacles examining X-ray films held up against a light box.
A clean anatomy textbook plate on aged paper with no people: two separate small neck vertebra bones drawn side by side with thin arrows showing how their edges fit together like puzzle pieces.
A medical chart on aged paper showing the outline of a standing man next to a tall measuring scale, an open army service record book beside it.
A close view of a large magnifying glass held over two fingerprint cards placed side by side on a desk, the ridge patterns matching.

Still life with no people, seen from above: a wooden table with three small items neatly placed apart, a pair of green socks, a coiled black thread, a small brass ear stud, each on a square of white cloth.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A small servant boy seen from behind standing before a seated police inspector in an empty house, the inspector leaning forward listening.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A small 1950s twin-propeller passenger aeroplane taking off from a simple airstrip, a few people waving.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A narrow old Bombay street with three-storey chawl buildings with wooden balconies, a horse carriage in the distance, two policemen in khaki standing at the doorway of a house, seen from across the street.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A wooden table with a wrist watch, a sheathed knife and a fountain pen laid out, a beam of light falling on the fountain pen.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. The red Indo-Saracenic high court building with domes, a long queue of people in 1950s dress waiting outside its gates.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Inside a 1950s courtroom, a lawyer in black gown and white bands arguing with a raised hand before a wooden jury box of twelve men.

South India in the early nineteen-fifties. Inside a courtroom, a grey-haired defence lawyer in a black gown speaking with an open hand, behind him in the wooden dock stand two adults, a slim man of thirty in a white shirt and a woman of twenty-three in a saree, both with lowered eyes.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. A young woman in a plain saree sitting across a table from a police officer in a bare room, shaking her head in refusal, eyes lowered.
South India in the early nineteen-fifties. An elderly Indian judge in black robes and spectacles seated on a high bench reading out a judgment from papers, courtroom silent.
A small roadside tea shop in Kerala among coconut palms, a couple seen from behind serving tea, green hills beyond.
A modern classroom of forensic science students in white coats, a teacher pointing at a drawing of neck bones on a blackboard.
Still life with no people: a large brass weighing scale of justice standing alone on a stone table against a dark teal wall, one pan lower than the other, a single beam of light from above.

Empty scene with no people: a large old bungalow with a wide stone courtyard at night under a full moon, long shadows of palm trees, one square patch of the courtyard floor glowing faintly, mysterious mood.
